ui.title: Workspace Restore
ui.intro: Each workspace keeps a list of apps. Restoring opens the ones that aren't open and moves the rest back. Nothing gets closed.
ui.restore-all-tooltip: Put every workspace back on its screen and move its apps there. Nothing gets closed.
ui.restore-all-tooltip-open: Put every workspace back on its screen and move its apps there. This also opens: {apps}. Nothing gets closed.
ui.restore-now-tooltip: Put this workspace back on its screen and move its apps there, opening any that aren't open. Nothing gets closed.
ui.add-app-tooltip: Pick an open window or an installed app to add to this workspace
ui.remove: Remove from this workspace's list (the app keeps running)
ui.at-login-tooltip: Restore this workspace automatically when you log in. Click to switch on or off.
ui.auto-add-tooltip: When you open an app on this workspace that isn't saved anywhere yet, add it to this list. It never removes anything. Click to switch on or off.
ui.keyword-tooltip: Restoring puts the {app} window whose title contains this word here. Press Enter to save.
ui.edit-failed: Couldn't change the list. It may have just changed; try again.
ui.search: Search open windows and installed apps
ui.open-windows-hint: Most reliable: remembers the exact command, browser profile or terminal command.
ui.installed-apps-hint: For apps that aren't open right now. Started from their app menu entry.

add-all-open.one: Add the window open on this workspace
add-all-open.other: Add all {count} windows open on this workspace

ui.add-again-tooltip: Already on this workspace's list. Add it again only if you use a second window of this app here.
ui.twice-here: {app} is on this list twice. If that's a mistake, remove one with ×.
ui.keyword-ask: To tell the windows apart, type a word from this window's title:
ui.listed-tooltip: This window is open on this workspace and already on its list
ui.already-listed: That window is already on this workspace's list.
ui.in-place-tooltip: Every app on this list is open here and the workspace is on its screen, so restoring would change nothing
ui.all-in-place-tooltip: Every workspace is already in place
ui.saved-on-tooltip: This workspace is saved on {saved}. Restoring moves it back there.
ui.move-screen-tooltip: Save {screen} as this workspace's screen, so restoring leaves it here
ui.move-app-tooltip: Move {app} from workspace {ws}'s list to this one
ui.add-also-tooltip: Add {app} here as well, keeping it on workspace {ws}'s list
ui.drag-tooltip: Drag onto another screen to move this workspace there now
ui.change-numbers-tooltip: Give workspaces new numbers or names. Apps stay on their screen.
ui.number-tooltip: New number for this workspace. Press Enter or Apply.
ui.apply-tooltip: Apply the new numbers and names. Windows, apps and settings keep their screen.
ui.state-here-tooltip: Open on this workspace, as saved
ui.state-elsewhere-tooltip: Saved here but open on workspace {ws}. Restoring moves it here.
ui.state-unsaved-tooltip: Open on this workspace but not on its list. Restoring leaves it alone.
ui.ghost: Saved on this screen, open on {now} now.
ui.move-back-tooltip: Move this workspace back to {screen} now
ui.legend-elsewhere: saved here, open on another workspace
ui.pinned-tooltip: A workspace rule in your Hyprland config pins this workspace to this screen, so it can't be moved to another one
ui.pinned-no-move: This workspace is pinned to its screen by a workspace rule in your Hyprland config.
ui.name-tooltip: Workspace name, shown in Hyprland too. Leave empty for the default.
ui.edge-here-tooltip: Every saved app is open here, on this screen
ui.edge-away-tooltip: This workspace or a saved app is somewhere else. Restoring brings it back.
ui.edge-closed-tooltip: A saved app is closed. Restoring opens it.
ui.edge-none-tooltip: No apps saved for this workspace
ui.legend-edge-away: workspace or a saved app is elsewhere

set-aside.one: put 1 window not on workspace {from}'s list on workspace {ws}
set-aside.other: put {count} windows not on workspace {from}'s list on workspace {ws}

ui.in-use: Another workspace is using number {ws}. Restoring skips this one.
ui.in-use-tooltip: This saved workspace closed, and a different workspace now has the number {ws}. Restoring leaves both alone until the other one closes.
ui.new-number-tooltip: Give this saved workspace a free number above the ones in use. The open workspace keeps its number.
ui.borrowed-hint: This workspace uses the number of your saved workspace {ws}. Nothing here gets saved, moved or restored.
ui.borrowed-ask: Workspace {ws} · is this your saved one?
ui.borrowed-ask-hint: It opened with one of saved workspace {ws}'s apps, but on another screen. Restoring and auto-add leave it alone until you answer.
ui.borrowed-app-tooltip: Open on this workspace, which isn't saved workspace {ws}
ui.borrowed-mine-tooltip: Treat this as saved workspace {ws}: restoring and auto-add work on it again
ui.skipped-in-use: skipped workspace {ws} (another workspace has the number)
ui.broken: A settings file couldn't be read, so it was set aside as {files} in ~/.local/state/workspace-restore/ and the plugin started fresh. Fix it and copy it back to get your old layout, or delete the copy to hide this.
